papers.title: The successor representation in high-risk drinking and alcohol-related contexts.
papers.reason: This is a human reinforcement-learning study modelling decision strategy use with successor representations, model-based control, and model-free control in addiction-relevant contexts.

papers.title: Instrumental Activities of Daily Living as a Mediator Between Cognition and Anti-Saccade Uncorrected Error Rate in CSVD: An Exploratory Analysis with Education Moderation Testing
papers.reason: This clinical CSVD study uses anti-saccade eye-movement measures as indicators of inhibitory control and relates them to cognition and daily function, although findings are exploratory and weak after correction.

papers.title: Strong mnemonic prediction errors increase cognitive control, attention, and arousal
papers.reason: This human EEG and pupillometry study directly links mnemonic prediction errors to frontal theta, posterior alpha, pupil-linked arousal, attention, and learning.

papers.title: Tumor lesions in the supplementary motor area may induce large-scale sensorimotor and cognitive network alterations— A functional and structural connectivity analysis
papers.reason: This neuroimaging study examines SMA-related structural and functional connectivity changes in cognitive networks, but it lacks direct executive-function behavioral testing.

papers.title: Poststroke sleep phenotypes and executive dysfunction: toward a sleep-network-executive framework
papers.reason: This synthesis proposes a mechanistic sleep-network-executive framework linking post-stroke sleep disturbance to frontoparietal, salience, and default-mode network dysfunction in executive impairment.

papers.title: Functional and Structural Neuroanatomic Correlates of Intraoperative Anesthetic Dose-Adjusted EEG Alpha Power Among Older Surgical Patients
papers.reason: The title indicates an anesthesia EEG and neuroanatomy study in older surgical patients with no clear connection to executive function, cognitive assessment, or computational modelling.

papers.title: Applying the Information-Motivation-Behavioral Skills Model to a Virtual Reality-Assisted Cognitive Health Education Intervention to Promote Screening Uptake: Qualitative Study.
papers.reason: This qualitative study concerns dementia and MCI screening education uptake rather than executive-function modelling, neural mechanisms, or biomarker-based cognitive assessment.

papers.title: A Virtual Reality-Based Cognitive Assessment Reveals an Association Between Regular Exercise and Multidimensional Cognitive Function in Community-Dwelling Middle-Aged Adults
papers.reason: The title suggests a digital cognitive assessment study, but the available information does not indicate executive-function modelling, clinical classification, eye tracking, EEG, or specific impairment detection.

papers.title: Reinforcement Learning for the Working Memory Controller
papers.reason: The title indicates a reinforcement learning model of working memory control, directly matching computational modelling of executive function.
